items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: I knew people like Malcolm Cowley

ctx.x: Did you have a sense that you were going to be a writer even before you went to Hamilton?

No. I was surrounded by writers growing up. And I mean I knew people like Malcolm Cowley, I knew Matthew Josephson, I never really knew Cummings but I’ve met him, but the writers I basically knew were people like my father and my uncle and various others, who were commercial writers. And they were always broke. My idea of a writer was a man in a bathrobe weeping limp, telling the man from the finance company that the check was in the mail. I mean that was my idea of what a writer was. But nonetheless it was a…

there was just a routine of several hours a day reading. And if the weather were bad and you didn’t have company to see or something, you might read all day long. Or if somebody were knitting and somebody else would be reading to them. You know it was just sort of books everywhere. And the great house that I was familiar with as a kid, my own family had no money, we were broke the whole time, but in my great aunt’s house there were just books everywhere. And in the house I grew up in there were books everywhere.…
